exploits.what: GET /notes/{id} checks login but not ownership (PUT does)
DELETE /notes/{id} has no authentication at all
DELETE /notes/{id} has no ownership check (follows from S2)
/files only rejects names starting with '..' or '/'; 'docs/../../secret/signing.key' escapes
PUT /me decodes the body into the whole User, so role and id can be set
admin token accepts prefixes and is timing-unsafe; require exact length plus subtle.ConstantTimeCompare or hmac.Equal
currentUser accepts a token without the required Bearer scheme
GET /search accepts any owner id from any authenticated user
POST /notes/import trusts note ids and owners, allowing overwrite of another user's note
a note title containing a newline forges a second audit-log record
lexical file checks do not stop a symlink below files from reaching outside the root
PUT /me reads an unbounded JSON body despite the documented 1 MiB limit
GET /integrations/{id} exposes another owner's endpoint and secret
DELETE /integrations/{id} has no authentication or ownership check
POST /integrations trusts owner_id instead of binding the creator
integration test fetches a loopback/private endpoint
integration test follows a redirect into a loopback/private endpoint
integration test reads an unbounded upstream response
integration export accepts another owner's id and includes secrets
secret rotation writes the new secret to the audit log
hook signature validation accepts a secret prefix
hook delivery has no required one-time nonce and accepts replay
